Container.Name: MC-Mod-Hub
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted Minecraft mod/addon search hub. Aggregates search results from Modrinth, CurseForge, PlanetMinecraft, 9Minecraft, and BetterBedrock into one searchable list, styled after a familiar category-browser layout (category pills, a "newest posts" notice board, sortable results table).
Every result and every mod detail page shows the required game edition (Java or Bedrock) and the game version(s) it supports - read directly from Modrinth/CurseForge's own API fields, and best-effort parsed from listing text on the scraped sites.
Browse by category (Mods, Modpacks, Resource/Texture Packs, Data Packs, Shaders, Maps/Worlds, Bedrock Add-Ons) without typing a search term, via category tiles or the sidebar.
Each mod's detail page also surfaces community discussion pulled from Reddit (since none of these platforms expose a public reviews API) with heuristic fake-review flags - duplicate text, generic praise, suspicious posting bursts - and YouTube videos about the mod with download links automatically extracted from each video's description.
CurseForge and YouTube API keys (both free, both optional but recommended) are entered and changed from the built-in admin portal after first boot at /admin.html - no file editing required, and no key ever needs to be baked into the container.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: minecraft mod addon search modrinth curseforge planetminecraft 9minecraft betterbedrock bedrock java edition modpack resourcepack shader
Container.Requires: Optional but recommended: a free CurseForge API key (console.curseforge.com) and YouTube Data API v3 key (Google Cloud Console) — both entered from the admin portal after first boot, not required to install or run the container.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port to access the web UI.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Persistent storage for the settings/config database (API keys, source toggles, admin password).

Config.Name: SESSION_SECRET
Config.Description: Random string used to sign admin login sessions. Set this to something unique.

Config.Name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Initial admin portal password. Only used the very first time the container starts (before the database exists) — change it from within the admin portal afterward.
